'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**[[Battle of Palma]]
***In the fourth day of a [[siege]] in [[Palma, Mozambique|Palma]], [[Mozambique]], several people are killed by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]-linked [[militant]]s. Local civilians are killed in streets and buildings, with reports of beheadings. A [[South Africa]]n man and a [[United Kingdom|British]] citizen are murdered after a hotel and an evacuation convoy are attacked; other foreigners are also suspected to have been killed. At least 21 [[Mozambique Defence Armed Forces|soldiers]] are shot dead while responding to the hotel attack. [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/islamist-rebels-kill-dozens-in-attack-on-mozambique-gas-project-s3fhl308z (''The Times'')] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/03/27/least-one-british-expatriate-killed-islamists-storm-mozambique/ (''The Telegraph'')]
***[[Islamism|Islamist]] militants have taken control of Palma after outnumbered [[Government of Mozambique|government]] forces withdraw from the town, according to security forces. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/mar/27/mozambique-several-dead-as-insurgents-seize-control-of-town (''The Guardian'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Three people are killed in a [[car bomb]]ing in [[Kandahar Province]]. [https://english.lokmat.com/international/car-bomb-blast-in-southern-afghanistan-kills-3-injures-4-security-officers/ (''Lokmat'')]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**More than 114 anti-[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] protesters are killed by the [[Tatmadaw|military]] as [[State Administration Council|junta]] leader [[Min Aung Hlaing]] celebrates Armed Forces Day and promises to "protect people and strive for democracy". The protests erupted across the country despite a warning by state television that protesters could be "shot in the head and back". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics/at-least-50-protesters-killed-in-myanmar-on-day-of-shame-for-armed-forces-idUSKBN2BJ01O (Reuters)] [https://www.wgauradio.com/news/world/myanmar-forces-kill-dozens-deadliest-day-since-coup/XA7SEILKTFAWG7YBOSMXCSHMKU/ (WGAU)]
*[[Colombia]]n Defense Minister Diego Molano accuses [[Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia|FARC]] [[FARC dissidents|splinter group]] Dagoberto Ramos Mobile Column of being responsible for yesterday's [[car bomb]]ing in [[Corinto, Cauca|Corinto]], [[Cauca Department]], that injured 43 people, eleven of whom were public officials. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-colombia-violence/colombia-accuses-farc-dissidents-over-car-bomb-attack-idUSKBN2BJ0IV?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 18 people are killed and 24 others are injured when an [[apartment complex]] building collapses in [[Cairo]], [[Egypt]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/27/building-collapse-in-egypts-cairo-leaves-5-dead-dozens-injured (Al Jazeera)]
*A [[Eurocopter_AS350_Écureuil#Specifications_(AS350_B3)|Eurocopter AS350B3]] helicopter crashes into a [[glacier]] near [[Anchorage]], [[Alaska]], killing five people, including [[Czechs|Czech]] [[billionaire]] [[Petr Kellner]]. One crew member survived and has been hospitalized. [https://www.reuters.com/article/alaska-helicopter-crash/five-killed-one-hurt-as-helicopter-crashes-at-alaska-glacier-idINKBN2BL0AP (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 community quarantines in the Philippines]]
****[[Enhanced community quarantine in Luzon]]
*****The [[Government of the Philippines|government]] announces that the [[Greater Manila Area]] will be placed under enhanced community [[quarantine]], which includes a curfew from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. local time, for one week from March 29 to April 4. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1412020/metro-manila-4-provinces-under-ecq-due-to-covid-19-surge-palace-2 (''Inquirer'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bhutan]]
****[[Bhutan]] launches their largest [[vaccination]] campaign against [[COVID-19]] using the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] that was received from [[India]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/bhutan-begins-biggest-covid-19-vaccination-drive-astrazeneca-14504644 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] reports a record 179 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,157. [https://www.khmertimeskh.com/50830878/179-cases-of-covid-19-positives-in-cambodia-marks-another-blow-in-fight-against-the-pandemic/ (''Khmer Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]]
*****[[First Minister of Northern Ireland|First Minister]] [[Arlene Foster]] receives her first dose of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/ireland/irish-news/north-s-first-minister-arlene-foster-receives-first-covid-19-vaccine-dose-1.4522028 (''The Irish Times'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wales]]
*****[[Wales]] lifts their "stay local" rules that have been imposed since December, allowing people to travel freely within the country. They also allow up to six people from two different households to meet and exercise outdoors, as well as resumption of organised outdoor activities and sports for people under the age of 18. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/wales-coronavirus-lockdown-stay-local-b1822685.html (''The Independent'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports 30,021 new cases in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total this year, thereby bringing its cumulative case total to 3,179,115. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1832856/middle-east (''Arab News'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Iran relations]]
**[[Iran–China 25-year Cooperation Program]]
***[[China]] and [[Iran]] sign a 25-year cooperation agreement at a live televised ceremony in [[Tehran]], following a two-day state visit by Chinese Foreign Minister [[Wang Yi (politician)|Wang Yi]]. The accord is expected to significantly increase Chinese investment in Iran, especially in the energy and infrastructure sectors. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-china/iran-china-sign-25-year-cooperation-agreement-idUSKBN2BJ0AD?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Afghanistan–United States relations]], [[Afghan peace process]]
***[[United States]] envoy to [[Afghanistan]] [[Zalmay Khalilzad]] visits [[Turkey]] in an effort to encourage parties to accelerate negotiations and end the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|conflict]]. [https://www.voanews.com/south-central-asia/us-envoy-afghanistan-heads-turkey-region-push-talks-end-conflict (Voice of America)]
*[[China–United States relations]], [[Canada–China relations]]
**China's [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] places sanctions against the chair and vice-chair of the [[United States Commission on International Religious Freedom]] and [[House of Commons of Canada|Canadian MP]] [[Michael Chong]]. Beijing’s sanctions followed those imposed by the United States, the European Union, Britain and Canada earlier this week for what they say are [[Xinjiang internment camps|violations of the rights]] of [[Uyghurs]] in [[Xinjiang]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-usa-canada/china-sanctions-u-s-and-canadian-bodies-over-xinjiang-idUSKBN2BJ0DW (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*One person is killed and six others are wounded in a [[mass stabbing]] in and around a public library in [[North Vancouver (city)|North Vancouver]], [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/north-vancouver-multiple-stabbed-1.5967155 (CBC News)]
*[[List of mass shootings in the United States in 2021]], [[Crime in Virginia]]
**A series of shootings occur on the oceanfront of [[Virginia Beach, Virginia]], Friday night. They consist of a [[mass shooting]] that left eight people injured; a subsequent, fatal shooting by a police officer; and an unrelated fatal shooting that occurred nearby. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/27/us/virginia-beach-shootings/index.html (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Voter suppression in the United States]], [[2020–21 Georgia state elections]]
**Changes to [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] voting laws which have been called [[voter suppression]] results in the [[MLB]] looking to proposals to [[boycott|move]] the [[MLB All-Star Game]] this July in [[Atlanta]]. Civil rights groups also urged the [[Professional Golfers' Association of America|PGA]] to pull the [[Masters Tournament]] at [[Augusta National Golf Club]]. [https://www.newsweek.com/georgia-voting-law-prompts-talks-moving-all-star-game-pulling-masters-augusta-1579196 (''Newsweek'')] 

*Thousands of women protest in [[Istanbul]] over [[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]]'s decision to withdraw from the [[Istanbul Convention]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-rights/turkish-women-protest-over-erdogans-decision-to-exit-domestic-violence-treaty-idUSKBN2BJ0J1?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Scottish National Party]] [[Member of parliament|MP]] [[Kenny MacAskill]] [[Defection|defects]] to the newly formed [[Scottish nationalism|Scottish nationalist]] [[Alba Party]], becoming the party's first MP in the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-scotland-politics-56550195 (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[COVID-19 misinformation by governments]]
**[[Facebook]] blocks the account of [[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan president]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] for spreading fake news related to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela|COVID-19 pandemic]] as well as alleged miraculous remedies to combat the disease. [https://www.elmundo.es/internacional/2021/03/27/605edc41fc6c8301758b4677.html (''El Mundo'')]
